clauses.text:
(d) Leave without compensation . If consistent with the public interest , leave of
absence for good reason may be granted without compensation for a longer time than
that stipulated in these regulations for leave of absence with pay; and in any case in
which leave of absence in one calendar year is to be extended to cover continuously
all or a portion of the leave for the ensuing year, the absence in the first year may be
supplemented in the discretion of the Secretary of State by leave without salary in
sufficient amount to cover the absence to the end of that calendar year, in order that
the leave with pay in the following year may be available .

own_original_text:
Executive Order
LEAVES OF ABSENCE , FOREIGN SERVICE
Paragraph (d), section 8, Chapter VI, Instructions to Diplomatic Officers , and
paragraph (d) , section 467 of the Consular Regulations of 1896, are hereby amended
to read as follows :
(d) Leave without compensation . If consistent with the public interest , leave of
absence for good reason may be granted without compensation for a longer time than
that stipulated in these regulations for leave of absence with pay; and in any case in
which leave of absence in one calendar year is to be extended to cover continuously
all or a portion of the leave for the ensuing year, the absence in the first year may be
supplemented in the discretion of the Secretary of State by leave without salary in
sufficient amount to cover the absence to the end of that calendar year, in order that
the leave with pay in the following year may be available .
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
March 26, 1932 .
[No. 5825]

versions.research_rationale: EO 5825 (signed 1932-03-26), read in full from the held official compilation text (Proclamations and Executive Orders: Herbert Hoover, vol. II, OFR/GPO 1974, printed page 1115, PDF page 344; jobs/ofr-compilations/output/texts/EO_5825.txt; grade official_compilation_high, OCR of the scan; the order predates the Federal Register). Status provisional NO, unchanged. The dossier's two clauses (lead 890-1163; paragraph (d) 1164-1820) cover the whole operative text; inventory confirmed. Deciding source: EO 8189 of 1939-07-05 (4 FR 2783, jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_8189.txt), 'The following executive orders are hereby revoked:' ... 'Executive Order No. 5825 dated March 26, 1932' (offsets 17110 and 17307-17353); no effective-date wording, so effective on signing 1939-07-05; both clauses first end then and whole_order_end is 1939-07-05. D6 / later events: the dossier chain lists EO 8189, 8190, 8191 and 8192 as direct namers. Only EO 8189 acts: the ACT records for EO 8190, 8191 and 8192 (their files' offsets 470-4370) are the same FR page 2785, whose top half is the end of EO 8189 with its revocation list (line 113 of each file); EOs 8190-8192 are other orders printed below it and do not mention EO 5825 in their own text. The draft's only proposal (1989 Codification table 'Revoked by EO 8189') is the same end. The earlier Lambertini III block (EO 7013 not held; EOs 6071-7531 not held as FR text) is answered as follows: EO 7013 is now held (APP transcription) and does not touch the leave paragraphs; the held APP, FR and OFR-compilation texts together cover every order number from 5826 to 8188 except 21 (6447, 6451, 6453, 6454, 6456, 6459, 6460, 6462, 6466, 6534-6536, 6758, 6762, 6765, 6851, 7004, 7007, 7008, 7087, 7373), and none of the held texts names EO 5825 or amends the leave paragraphs; those 21 are a disclosed residual gap with no lead pointing to them. Unnamed earlier candidates (EO 7409 effective 1936-07-01; EO 7845 effective 1938-01-01, both general annual-leave regulations with inconsistency revocations) are disclosed per clause under the unnamed-instruments ruling and do not move the end. The OFR catalog search has a coverage warning (catalog starts 1937), so it is used only with the U.S. Code and eCFR searches (no current-law citation) and the scans above. Quotations in this claim are copied from the held OCR text layers with line breaks, soft hyphens and letter-spacing normalized; the exact spans are at the stated offsets. savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 8189 (held official FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_8189.txt, 4 FR 2783-2785, PDF pages 1-3, read for this purpose: the enacting sentence, the new Chapter IV including IV-11 'Leaves of absence. Officers and employees of the Foreign Service may avail themselves of statutory leave subject to regulations prescribed by the Secretary of State governing the granting of such leave.', the 'Cancellation of Regulations' list, the 'Revocation of Executive Orders' list and the signature): no savings, pending-matter or 'shall not affect' wording; the replacement rule IV-11 is new law under EO 8189, not a continuation of EO 5825. Own-residual check, reading EO 5825 in full (Hoover PEO vol. II, printed page 1115, jobs/ofr-compilations/output/texts/EO_5825.txt offsets 890-1820): it restated one regulation paragraph on leave without compensation; it created no office, fund or vested right, and individual leave grants made under it were completed administrative acts. Nothing of the order outlives the revocation. Bounded search: the order and EO 8189 read in full; by-number scans for '5825' of all held FR order texts (hits: EO 8189 and the FR page it shares with EO 8190, 8191 and 8192; EO 9973, 10003 and 10829 are FR document or page numbers and EO 11152 and 13050 are digits inside file hashes), of the held APP texts and of the held OFR compilation texts (only EO 8189 names it); a subject scan of the held APP texts for 'section 467', 'leave without compensation' and 'Chapter VI, Instructions' (only EO 5642 of 1931, the earlier text that EO 5825 restated, and EO 8189); the three machine searches read with their scope notes.
